doc.title: Ira Gitler interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Coltrane's sound and his influence
summary: Coltrane's distinct sound and powerful influence even on musicians with established styles.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: It was still there in the sound.

Yeah. He had a distinct sound, there’s no doubt about that. And that’s something every musician strives for is to get that recognizable, that individual sound. And he had it of course, and everybody who’s coming behind him figuring boy this sounds good, I’m going to play like that, which is what always happens. Some did it and brought something of themselves to it and others didn’t.
Some people say it’s not wise to look for a man’s predecessor amongst his imitators.

Well you know sometimes he influenced people who already had established styles too. He was such a powerful force. It wasn’t just the people who came up behind him, it was some of the people that were already there. And then they had to come to a maybe a rapprochement between what they had been before they heard him and what he gave them and then they kind of sorted it out and then went back to being themselves and retaining something of him.
